title: How to Write a Sales Pitch: Tips + Examples
summary: Learn how to craft the perfect sales pitch with examples, tips, and strategies. Discover how to start a pitch, personalize it, and improve your sales success.
body_text: A great sales pitch can be the difference between landing a deal or losing out to the competition. It’s not just about presenting your product or service—it’s about connecting with your audience and showing them exactly how you can solve their problems. As a sales rep, crafting a sales or client pitch that resonates with your audience isn’t just about creating good talking points. It requires an in-depth understanding of your audience, drafting a message around their unique needs, delivering it clearly, and making your offer irresistible. Below, we’ll explain how to write a sales pitch and highlight the best sales pitch examples. Before we get into sales pitch examples, let’s review what a sales pitch is. What is a sales pitch? A sales pitch is a persuasive conversation. It’s where you start the conversation with customers and introduce your product or service to them. The goal is to convince a prospect it’s the right solution for their needs. Here’s an example of a sales pitch: Say you’re trying to sell an old bike on a classifieds website or a cold call, you wouldn’t just say: ‘Here’s a bike; it’s for sale.’ You highlight the bike’s features—how it’s great for commuting, how smoothly the gears shift, why it’s in excellent condition, and anything else that makes it clear why buyers or potential prospects should choose your bike over others. The same ideal or concept is true in the business world. A sales pitch is a sales rep’s chance to quickly grab someone’s attention and park their interest. It’s also a chance to showcase your value proposition, and lead customers’ to the conclusion that your product or service is exactly what they’re looking for. If your sales team sells software that streamlines billing for doctor’s offices, for example, your pitch might focus on how it saves time or reduces data errors. You might also highlight how it increases revenue, all while making life easier for busy healthcare professionals. A sales pitch, at its core, is about showing the value of what you’re offering, not just listing features. The goal of the sales pitch is to understand what your audience cares about and speak directly to those specific needs. When it comes to sales pitches, there’s a few different types and templates to choose from, including an elevator pitch, consultative pitch, and product-focused pitch. Depending on the situation and the person you’re talking to, you’ll want to switch things up. Below we’ll discuss each of these three common sales pitches and how your salespeople can use them in their talk tracks, sales decks, or other sales approaches. Elevator Pitch: Your High-Level Overview The elevator pitch is all about being short and concise. Picture this: you’re stuck in an elevator with a potential client , and you have about 30 seconds to grab their attention. That’s the essence of the elevator pitch—it’s a short, but compelling introduction that highlights the most important parts of your product or service as well as your value proposition. It’s not meant to be an in-depth explanation of your product but rather to spark some interest in your product. An elevator pitch is particularly helpful for salespeople if they’re cold calling. Or in initial presentations with prospects. They’re also a great way to start a sales deck. For example, a good elevator pitch for an app that helps organize team projects could be: “Our app helps busy teams keep things organized by providing them with a simple, all-in-one place to track tasks, deadlines, and communication, saving hours every week.” The goal of an elevator pitch is to leave your customers wanting to know more, not to close the deal right then and there. Product-Focused Pitch: It’s All About Your Product A product-focused pitch goes deeper into what you’re actually selling. It’s where you explain more about how exactly your product works, its features, why it’s better than the competition, and give a look into pricing. A sales pitch example could be this: If you or your sales reps are selling a new coffee maker, you might emphasize how it brews coffee faster, has customizable settings for different tastes, or uses eco-friendly materials. This type of pitch is ideal when your prospect is already somewhat interested in your product, or when you’re talking to someone who’s researching similar products. Remember, tailor this sales pitch to someone’s specific, unique needs and their pain points—focus on the features that are most relevant to them. Consultative Pitch: The Personal Approach to Selling Another sales pitch example is the consultative pitch. This type of pitch takes a more personalized, problem-solving approach with your potential customers or prospects. Rather than leading with what your product does, you start off by asking questions to understand the prospect’s pain points, then tailor your sales pitch to show how well, fast, or cost-effectively your products solve those issues. A consultative pitch is the perfect approach if you’re wanting to build trust because it’s not just about pushing a product; it’s about listening to your customers and offering a solution that actually solves their problems. For example, if salespeople are selling a marketing service, they might start by asking questions like: ‘What challenges are you facing in your current advertising strategy ?’ Then you could explain how your service can address those specific issues. By focusing on their unique challenges, sales reps make it clear you’re offering more than just a generic solution—you’re providing something that can actually make a difference for them and solve their pain points. How To Write a Sales Pitch in 5 Steps Now that we’ve talked about what a sales pitch is and the different types, let’s discuss how to write a sales pitch or a sales deck. Reel Them in with a Hook. Start your sales pitch with something that resonates with your prospect’s pain points or interests. You could use a bold statement, a thought-provoking question, or a relevant statistic. For example, sales reps selling time-management tools could start with: “Did you know the average employee spends two hours a day just organizing their tasks?” A hook creates instant relevance and curiosity. Understand Your Prospect’s Needs and Acknowledge Them: Next, sales reps need to show they understand the prospect’s challenges . This step is especially important in consultative pitches, but it applies to all sales pitch ideas. Ask questions or make observations that demonstrate you’ve done your homework and are actively interested in their problems and solving them. For instance, the conversation could start with: “I noticed that your team is struggling with keeping deadlines on track. Does that sound familiar?” It helps build rapport and shows your pitch isn’t just about pushing a product—but actually finding a solution. Clearly Show Why Your Product is the Best: Now it’s time to talk about what you’re offering. Keep this part simple, direct, and focused on your product’s benefits. Your sales pitch shouldn’t just rattle off features—explain how those features translate into real value. If you’re selling a CRM system, rather than saying: “Our CRM tracks customer interactions,” in a cold call, say: “Our CRM gives your sales team a 360-degree view of each customer, so they can close deals faster and build stronger relationships.” Highlight how your product will make their life easier and solve their problems. Address Customers’ Concerns Right off the Bat: Make sure you anticipate any questions or issues your prospect might have and address them before they bring them up in the conversation. If you know they might be worried about cost, explain how the value you’re offering justifies the price. If they’re hesitant about time constraints, show them how easy and quick it will be to implement. For example, your sales deck or pitch could address issues around budget by saying: “I get you’re on a tight budget, but by streamlining your processes with our tool, you’ll actually save money long-term by reducing inefficiencies.” End with Something that Encourages Action: The closing of your sales pitch idea is just as important as the opening. End with a prompt that encourages the prospect to take the next step and move beyond their pain points. Whether it’s scheduling a meeting with you or signing up for a free trial, make it easy for them to say “yes.” Be specific and confident as well. For example, salespeople could say: “Let’s set up a demo next week so you can see how our product works.” Or “I’ll send over the contract for you to review today.” A strong call to action gives your prospect a clear direction and keeps the momentum going. 6 Sales Pitch Examples and Templates You Can Use for Inspiration To give you a better idea of what a successful sales pitch looks like, let’s walk through some of the best sales pitch examples in a few different contexts. These pitch examples can help you know how to start a sales pitch on your own and boost salespeople’s chances of success. Slack: “Be less busy.” Slack’s simple tagline cuts straight to the heart of what their product does. It shows how the tool makes work more efficient and isn’t as overwhelming. The sales pitch is short and benefits-driven, appealing to busy professionals who want to save time and be more productive. Here’s the takeaway from Slack’s sales pitch: Keep your message simple. Focus on the clear benefits. Address the audience’s pain points directly, and use language that evokes an emotional response from your prospects. Airbnb: “Belong anywhere.” Airbnb isn’t just selling a place to stay; they’re selling an experience—feeling at home anywhere in the world. Their pitch taps into the deep human desire to connect with others and to belong somewhere, offering travelers a unique, local, and personal experience when traveling. Make sure you use a value proposition that speaks to someone’s deeper emotional needs. A compelling pitch isn’t just selling a product; it sells the experience and the feelings associated with it. Tesla: “Accelerating the world’s shift to sustainable energy.” Tesla’s sales pitch is more than about selling electric cars—it’s a bold vision for the future. This pitch clearly articulates the company’s mission and appeals to people who want to be part of something bigger than just a car purchase. Take some inspiration from Tesla and ensure your sales pitch is about more than just the product. If you have a bigger vision, make sure you communicate it in your conversations with prospects. Remember: People want to be part of something meaningful. Dropbox: “Simplify your life.” Dropbox’s pitch is centered on solving a very simple problem among businesses: file storage and sharing. By framing their product as a way to simplify everyday tasks, they appeal to people looking for an easy, no-fuss solution. Your sales pitch idea should do the same—focus on how your product makes the customer’s life easier. A sales pitch that is centered on benefits rather than features is often more compelling. Dollar Shave Club: “Our blades are f*ing great” Dollar Shave Club’s pitch is both humorous and bold. By using everyday, simple language and humor with their prospects, they disrupt the typical razor pitch template and are seen as memorable in today’s noisy marketing world. They also back it up with a strong, memorable slogan and direct value (great blades at a low price). The lesson: Don’t be afraid to inject personality into your pitch—whether it’s in your sales deck or cold calls. Humor, when done right, can be an easy way to make your pitch or conversation more memorable and resonate more with your prospects. Nike: “Just do it.” Nike’s iconic slogan doesn’t focus on specific products; instead, it motivates and inspires people to go beyond their limits and achieve greatness in whatever physical goals they’re chasing. It’s a call to action that really sticks with athletes and non-athletes alike. The takeaway: A short, impactful, and concise pitch that resonates with people’s aspirations can be more effective than one that focuses solely on the product. Increasing Your Sales with Podium To truly boost your sales, it’s not enough just to have a great client pitch . It’s all about the right tools—ones that connect you with your customers in meaningful ways. That’s where Podium can help. With Podium, you can seamlessly engage and connect with your customers across all your channels—including social media, text messaging, web chat, and email . By streamlining communication, nurturing leads, and responding quickly, Podium not only increases your efficiency but also boosts audience trust in your brand, opening the door for more sales . Plus, these insights give you the direction needed to create a more personalized sales pitch that sticks with your prospects. Ready to see Podium in action? Watch a demo today .

title: RTX's Collins Aerospace opens UK Engineering Center of Excellence to advance next-generation aircraft systems
summary: Modular and scalable test facility drives innovation for electric thrust reverser actuation systems WOLVERHAMPTON, England, July 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Collins Aerospace, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, announced today its Engineering Center of Excellence in Wolverhampton, U.K. is fully operational, advancing next-generation electric thrust reverser actuation systems (elecTRAS™). The CoE is home to a new state-of-the-art, modular and scalable test facility designed to facilitate innovation in aircraft actuation system design, testing and certification. With a more streamlined solution, elecTRAS supports the elimination of actuation hydraulic interfaces and fluids and facilitates a 15-20% reduction of the nacelle actuation weight at the integrated aircraft system level. Wolverhampton's advanced testing capabilities simulate real-world conditions for aircraft components, actuators, subsystems, and full systems. By integrating early-stage test results into system analysis, potential issues are resolved quickly, reducing delays and enhancing distinctive design scalability for future applications.
body_text: RTX's Collins Aerospace opens UK Engineering Center of Excellence to advance next-generation aircraft systems July 09, 2026 Share this article on Facebook Share this article on Twitter Share this article on LinkedIn Share this article via email Modular and scalable test facility drives innovation for electric thrust reverser actuation systems WOLVERHAMPTON, England , July 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Collins Aerospace, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, announced today its Engineering Center of Excellence in Wolverhampton, U.K. is fully operational, advancing next-generation electric thrust reverser actuation systems (elecTRAS™). The CoE is home to a new state-of-the-art, modular and scalable test facility designed to facilitate innovation in aircraft actuation system design, testing and certification. With a more streamlined solution, elecTRAS supports the elimination of actuation hydraulic interfaces and fluids and facilitates a 15-20% reduction of the nacelle actuation weight at the integrated aircraft system level. Wolverhampton's advanced testing capabilities simulate real-world conditions for aircraft components, actuators, subsystems, and full systems. By integrating early-stage test results into system analysis, potential issues are resolved quickly, reducing delays and enhancing distinctive design scalability for future applications. "Our Engineering Center of Excellence reflects RTX's commitment to delivering innovative, efficient and cost-effective solutions for the aerospace industry," said Ajay Mahajan, president of Advanced Structures at Collins Aerospace. "This unique modular approach supports the industry's transition to more-electric systems, aligning with original equipment manufacturers' forward-looking goals while improving fuel efficiency, operational performance, and ease of maintenance." The Wolverhampton test capability spans from modules to integrated systems. This allows for scalability and interchangeability, reducing development time and cost while enabling the facility to support multiple programs and system variants. Co-located elecTRAS systems and nacelle actuation design expertise streamlines development and fosters efficient collaboration. Highly skilled engineers at the facility are driving innovation in electric systems, smart algorithms, and motor control architecture, while continuing to support current fleets. Already in use on the Airbus A350 family, Collins' elecTRAS technology has logged more than 15 million flight hours and 2.2 million flight cycles on more than 700 aircraft as of 2025. An engineer conducts electrical testing on elecTRAS™ control components to ensure the system operates safely and reliably. Digital Image Correlation (DIC) captures detailed 3-D motion and strain data on elecTRAS™ components, enabling engineers to validate the simulation models used to analyze structural integrity and performance. Engineers at the elecTRAS™ Centre of Excellence in Wolverhampton, UK are advancing electric thrust reverser actuation technology to support the development of next-generation aircraft systems. About Collins Aerospace Collins Aerospace, an RTX business, provides advanced aerospace and defense solutions across avionics, aircraft interiors, aerostructures and engine components, mission systems, and power and control systems. Our global employees are dedicated to delivering innovative technologies to enhance aircraft performance, passenger comfort, operational safety and reliability. About RTX With more than 180,000 global employees, we push the limits of technology and science to redefine how we connect and protect our world. With industry-leading capabilities, we advance aviation, engineer integrated defense systems for operational success, and develop next-generation technology solutions and manufacturing to help global customers address their most critical challenges. The company, with 2025 sales of more than $88 billion, is headquartered in Arlington, Virginia. For questions or to schedule an interview, please contact [email protected] . July 28, 2026 The contact center AI landscape is evolving fast and so are the expectations of the enterprises navigating it. As AI becomes central to how service organizations operate, one question keeps coming up: who decides which AI powers your agents? For too long, the answer has been dictated by the platforms themselves. Organizations running Five9 with Salesforce deserve better. They want the flexibility to choose the solution that best fits their existing investments, their agent workflows, and their long-term business goals. That's exactly what Five9 Fusion for Salesforce delivers, providing choice in which AI powers your agents. A partnership built on over 15 years of trust Five9 and Salesforce have been working together for more than 15 years, supporting over 1,000 shared customers and 160,000+ service agents globally. Five9 Fusion for Salesforce is the natural evolution of that collaboration with a deeply integrated, AI-elevated solution that combines Five9's real-time system of action with Salesforce CRM to create a unified, intelligent foundation for customer experience. But Five9 Fusion for Salesforce is more than a technical integration. It represents a shared commitment to giving joint customers the tools, flexibility and AI capabilities they need to deliver modern service experiences without forcing them into a one-size-fits-all approach. At the heart of this integration is a principle every enterprise deserves: choice. Specifically, the choice of which AI solution powers your agents' real-time experience. What are your AI agent assist options with Five9 Fusion for Salesforce? Not every organization is in the same place on its AI journey, and there's no single right answer when it comes to agent assist. Your approach depends on where your team is today. The tools that are already in place, the workflows your agents rely on and the outcomes you're working toward. With Five9 Fusion for Salesforce, customers can choose the path that makes the most sense for them. Option 1: Five9 AI Agent Assist For organizations that want a best-in-class agent assist experience within Salesforce , Five9 AI Agent Assist delivers everything agents need to perform at their best in real time, right within their service console. Five9 AI Agent Assist empowers every role with AI by: Surfacing real-time guidance cards and checklists Automatically generating post-call summaries Providing live in-call transcription With Five9 AI Agent Assist as their fingertips, contact centers can: Free agents from manual notetaking Reduce average handle time, Accelerate after-call work Improve first contact resolution Enable agents to stay focused on the customer rather than scrambling for the right answer For new agents, real-time coaching accelerates time to proficiency. For experienced agents, it surfaces the right information at exactly the right moment. The result is a more confident, more efficient and more empathetic agent experience. Option 2: Einstein for Service, powered by Five9 TranscriptStream For organizations that have already invested in Salesforce Einstein for Service and want to activate its full potential within their contact center, Five9 TranscriptStream is the bridge that makes it possible. Five9 TranscriptStream is a real-time transcription streaming API that captures live voice call data and streams it directly into Salesforce grounding Einstein for Service AI features including Next Best Actions, Reply Recommendations and automated Call Summaries with live, accurate conversation data. Rather than processing audio after the fact, TranscriptStream delivers transcription as the conversation unfolds, word by word, in real time. This distinction matters. It means Einstein for Service can act on what the customer is saying right now surfacing contextually relevant guidance mid-call, not in a post-call report. Agents benefit from AI-powered recommendations that are anchored in the live conversation, while supervisors and managers gain a richer, more complete view of interaction quality and customer sentiment across the contact center. Here’s why this flexibility matters In the era of AI, vendor lock-in is a real and growing risk. Enterprises are making significant investments in AI tooling across their CRM, contact center and workforce platforms, and they need those investments to work together, not compete with each other. Five9 Fusion for Salesforce was built with that reality in mind. Whether your team is standardized on Five9 AI Agent Assist or you're leveraging Einstein for Service as your Salesforce-native AI layer, the integration supports your strategy without forcing you to compromise. You get a future-ready foundation that meets your business where it is today and scales with you as your AI approach evolves. The right AI for your agents is the one that fits your business. With Five9 Fusion for Salesforce , that decision stays yours. title: How to Get an Internship at TikTok 2026-2027
summary: TikTok internship guide with 261 open roles, current pay examples, timing, role-specific application proof, and interview preparation for 2026–2027.
body_text: Live TikTok internship openings 261 open TikTok internships · 7 representative roles shown · checked July 28, 2026 Frontend Software Engineer Project Intern BS/MS · San Jose · Fall 2026 · $45–$60/hr Product Solutions and Operations Project Intern BS/MS · San Jose · Summer or Fall 2026 · $35–$55/hr Product Manager Intern, TikTok Search BS/MS · San Jose · Fall 2026 · $35/hr Creator Operations Project Intern, TikTok LIVE BS/MS · Los Angeles · term varies · $23.75/hr Social Media Operations and User Campaigns Intern BS/MS · San Jose · Fall 2026 · $25/hr Logistics Operations Project Intern, TikTok Shop Bachelor’s · Madrid · Fall 2026 · pay not posted Applied Scientist Intern, Recommendation AI Lab PhD · San Jose · Fall 2026 · $60/hr Explore all current TikTok openings on Simplify → What You Should Know About TikTok Internships Pick the program before the role. Standard undergraduate and Master's, MBA, Project Intern, PhD, and Global Frontier Tech routes carry different eligibility, duration, and recruiting rules. Choosing wrong costs an application slot. Spend the two-position limit deliberately. Standard Early Career candidates may apply to two positions per program in each January–June and July–December period. PhD and Project Intern openings sit outside that cap. Attach your evidence to a product surface. A recommendation experiment, a performance number, a Shop operating fix, or a creator growth analysis beats stated enthusiasm for the app. TikTok Internships at a Glance Question Verified answer What is open now? 261 TikTok internships across nine countries, checked July 28, 2026. Who can apply? Current students. Class year, degree, and work-authorization rules vary by requisition. How many can I apply to? Two Early Career positions per program per half-year. PhD and Project Intern roles are exempt. Are internships paid? Yes. Just under half list a pay figure, nearly all hourly. Use the requisition's number. When Do TikTok Internship Applications Open? TikTok's Early Careers guidance describes a cycle, not a launch day. Most opportunities open from August, recruiting usually concludes by May, and applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. PhD and Project Intern opportunities recruit year-round. What we see on Simplify matches that. TikTok has posted internships every month since August 2025, with the heaviest bursts in August, January, March, and July. Most of what is open today starts in summer 2026, with a smaller fall group behind it. If you are mapping a longer runway, the Summer 2027 internship application timeline covers how the cycle tends to move. 📅 A season tag is not a deadline. TikTok reviews applications as they arrive, so a fall role posted in July can close before an equivalent role posted in September opens. Apply when the matching requisition appears, not on a date you picked in advance. What Internships Does TikTok Offer? TikTok's early-career hiring runs across six official team groups: technology, product, e-commerce, design, marketing and global operations, and advertising. The five paths below are where the current openings sit. Legal, finance, people, and support hire interns under the same rules, with far fewer openings. Software Engineering and Infrastructure TikTok's technology organization covers recommendation and search algorithms, the systems that store and deliver video at scale, client engineering on the iOS, Android, and web apps, and the privacy and security infrastructure underneath. Interns join one of those teams rather than TikTok engineering in general, and the team decides whether your work is measured in playback latency, model serving cost, or crash-free sessions. Best proof: a system you can trace end to end, with tests, a performance number you moved, and one trade-off you can defend. AI, Machine Learning, and Data Recommendation is TikTok's central technical problem and most of this work sits close to it: candidate retrieval, ranking, search relevance, ads prediction, and the experimentation systems that decide whether a change helped. Research groups work further out, reached through two separate routes, a PhD internship and the Global Frontier Tech program, the only part of early careers TikTok itself calls highly selective. Best proof: one experiment somebody else could reproduce, with your baseline, the metric you chose and why, and a limitation you did not solve. Product, Product Solutions, and Design Product interns own a named surface rather than the app as a whole: Search, LIVE, Shop, ads products, the short-video core, or Trust and Safety tooling. Product solutions is a distinct job sitting between customers and engineering, turning friction advertisers and sellers keep hitting into requirements a team can build. Design covers research, interaction work, and the systems keeping a product coherent across dozens of markets. Best proof: one case study with the problem, your evidence, the options you rejected, the metric you moved. TikTok Shop, Commerce, Creator, and LIVE Operations TikTok's fastest-moving commercial surface, and the one applicants understand least. E-commerce teams run seller and category growth, supply chain and logistics, marketplace governance, and the data science behind all three. Creator and LIVE teams recruit and grow agencies and run content and monetization programs. Almost every role is scoped to one country, and postings outside the United States frequently require fluency in that market's language. Best proof: an operating result with a number on it, and the constraint you worked inside. Advertising, Marketing, Sales, and Business Strategy The largest share of TikTok's current openings sits on the commercial side, and it is the most open to non-technical majors. The work splits between the ad products themselves, the agency and account teams who sell and service them, the marketing teams running campaigns on TikTok's own channels, and the strategy teams choosing which markets and formats to push next. Titles vary more here than anywhere else, so read the responsibilities. Best proof: a campaign, forecast, or growth decision with a measured outcome. Software Engineering and Infrastructure The work. These teams are organized by system. One tunes the models that pick your next video; another keeps the delivery pipeline fast enough that the video is already buffered; another ships the client that renders it on a mid-range Android phone where data is expensive. The constraint you inherit depends entirely on which you join. Who fits and what to show. Postings generally ask for computer science or a closely related degree, and current openings span Bachelor's through PhD. Lead with one project you can walk from requirement to validation, with your contribution explicit. Explain the tests, the edge case that broke it, and the trade-off you chose. A small system you can discuss in depth beats a large repository you cannot. Current openings, pay, and preparation. The Frontend Software Engineer Project Intern role in San Jose lists $45 to $60 an hour. Technical roles may include an online assessment, and TikTok publishes a preparation kit for it. AI, Machine Learning, and Data The work. Most machine learning interns work on ranking and retrieval for the feed, search, or ads, where a small offline gain has to survive an online test before anyone believes it. Data science roles sit beside them, defining metrics and running the experiments that decide what ships. Who fits and what to show. One reproducible experiment beats a list of coursework. Give the baseline, the metric and why you chose it over the obvious alternative, an error analysis showing where the model failed, and a limitation you could not fix. Say what it would change about a product decision, because that is what an interviewer will ask. Current openings, pay, and preparation. The Applied Scientist Intern role with the Recommendation AI Lab lists $60 an hour for PhD candidates. Build your walkthrough around method and trade-offs rather than the headline number. Product, Product Solutions, and Design The work. A product intern is handed a surface and a problem on it: why creators abandon a flow in LIVE, what people search for and do not find, how a seller decides to run an ad. Product solutions works the other direction, turning friction that advertisers and sellers report into something engineering can prioritize. Who fits and what to show. No single major dominates. What separates candidates is one case you can narrate as a decision: the problem, the evidence, the options you rejected, the metric you chose, and what changed after launch. Bring a portfolio only when the posting asks, and label team work honestly. Current openings, pay, and preparation. Product Manager Intern on TikTok Search lists $35 an hour; Product Solutions and Operations lists $35 to $55. Practice ambiguous problems and metric selection. No universal case round is promised. TikTok Shop, Commerce, Creator, and LIVE Operations The work. Operations interns own a mechanism, not a ticket queue. That might mean working out why sellers in one category churn after their first campaign, shortening a fulfillment step that costs a day, or building the onboarding path that takes a LIVE agency from signed to earning. Teams are organized by market, so what works in Spain may be irrelevant in Indonesia. Who fits and what to show. Business, supply chain, industrial engineering, and analytics backgrounds all land here, as do candidates with real operating experience from a student venture or a job. Show one improvement with a number attached, and be honest about the constraint you worked inside. Current openings, pay, and preparation. Creator Operations Project Intern on TikTok LIVE in Los Angeles lists $23.75 an hour; the Madrid Logistics Operations Project Intern role lists no pay. Learn the market before you interview. Advertising, Marketing, Sales, and Business Strategy The work. This organization turns attention into revenue, and interns sit at identifiable points in that chain. Ad product teams decide what advertisers can buy. Agency and account teams sell it and keep it working. Marketing teams run TikTok's own campaigns, measured on the same platform mechanics as any creator. Strategy picks the next market or format. Who fits and what to show. This is the widest door for business, marketing, and economics students, and the one where enthusiasm most often substitutes for evidence. Bring a campaign, forecast, or growth decision with a measured outcome, and name what you would change. Current openings, pay, and preparation. Social Media Operations and User Campaigns in San Jose lists $25 an hour. Be ready to discuss TikTok as a business rather than an app: how it makes money, who it competes with for budget, and what changed in the last year. How Hard Is It to Get a TikTok Internship, and What Does It Pay? TikTok publishes no acceptance rate, applicant count, or cohort size, so treat any figure quoted elsewhere as unsourced. The one official selectivity claim covers Global Frontier Tech. That label does not extend to the rest of Early Careers. The application limit tells you more than a rate would: two positions per program per half-year means the binding constraint is your fit, not your volume. On pay, just under half the open internships list a figure, nearly all hourly. Current U.S. openings run from $23.75 an hour for creator operations in Los Angeles to $60 for a PhD applied scientist role in San Jose. The Madrid logistics opening lists nothing. There is no single TikTok intern rate; the number that counts is on the requisition. How Do You Apply for a TikTok Internship? Choose the program and region. Decide between standard undergraduate and Master's hiring, MBA, Project Intern, PhD, or Global Frontier Tech, then read the regional page. Americas internships run 12 weeks; APAC formats range from 12 weeks to a semester or longer. Treat the two-position limit as a fit test. Shortlist the two roles where your evidence is strongest, not the two that sound most appealing. PhD and Project Intern openings are exempt, which is a reason to look at them. Name the surface, then tailor to it. Pick the surface, work out what problem that team has, and lead your resume with the project, metric, experiment, or operating decision that matches. Standard roles commonly open from August into the following May, Project Intern and PhD roles appear year-round, and review is rolling throughout. Prepare for the step the role actually has. Technical candidates should expect a possible online assessment. Everyone should follow the requisition rather than a process described in a forum. Keep TikTok's two-position limit working in your favor. Compare the few roles that best match your evidence, tailor each resume version, and track assessments and recruiter follow-ups in one place. TikTok describes its process as resume screening, an online assessment where applicable, hiring-team interviews, and an offer if selected. The assessment is not universal, so read the requisition first. Role-specific preparation sits with each path above. For the behavioral round, TikTok's interview guidance points at four things: know TikTok, know the role, know your relevant experience, and follow current news, trends, and competitors. Specific examples land better than rehearsed narratives, and the behavioral interview preparation guide covers how to keep them that way. ⚠️ Do not prepare for one universal TikTok loop. The hiring path varies by team and position, and round counts posted in forums are not process evidence. Let the recruiter and the requisition tell you the format. Frequently Asked Questions About TikTok Internships Is it hard to get a TikTok internship? TikTok publishes no acceptance rate, so nobody can honestly give you a number. What is documented is the constraint: two applications per program each half-year, which rewards fit over volume. Only Global Frontier Tech is officially called highly selective. Do TikTok interns get paid? Yes. Just under half the openings list a figure, nearly all hourly, ranging from $23.75 an hour for a Los Angeles creator operations role to $60 for a PhD applied scientist role in San Jose. The exact number sits on each posting. When do TikTok internship applications open? Most open from August, with recruiting usually concluding by May. PhD and Project Intern opportunities run year-round. TikTok reviews on a rolling basis, so apply when a matching requisition appears rather than waiting for a published date. What's the easiest way to get a TikTok internship? No shortcut, but there is a cheaper path: pick the program and surface that already fit your evidence instead of applying to whatever is open. A recommendation-systems project points at the AI lab roles; a campaign result points at growth and operations. How many TikTok internships can I apply for? Two per program during each application period, running January through June and July through December. PhD and Project Intern roles are exempt. TikTok's FAQ notes the limit can apply across TikTok and its affiliates globally, so applications elsewhere in the group may count. Are TikTok and ByteDance internships the same? No. Separate requisitions under separate employers, and this guide counts only TikTok. ByteDance lists 88 internships of its own, kept separate throughout. The one place they connect is the application limit, which TikTok says can apply across affiliates. Which Internship Guides Should I Read Next? title: The Old Course in Reverse | YETI® Stories
summary: Todd “TC” Schuster of No Laying Up visits the world's oldest golf course — and plays it backward.
body_text: Somehow, by the time we’d gotten out to the far end of the course, the wind had switched and was now hurting on our right, heavy off the North Sea. Admiral’s bunker was right in the landing area for where we wanted to hit our drives about 225 yards off the tee. There was plenty of room past that to the right, but it was a matter of whether we could actually get past the gorse and scrub with how strong the wind was. Lay back too much and you’re worried about going too far into one of the narrowest, most well-protected greens in golf. Navigate the tee shot, and you’re faced with an uphill shot over the Hill bunker with the Strath bunker guarding the right side and a steep depression on the left. When approached, as I have many times, from the right at a 45-degree angle, these obstacles pose more of an objective challenge, and the green, while shallow, is an ample target at 40 yards wide. But in reverse, and with an extra shot as a par four, each hazard and element compounded the challenge. Our minds in overdrive and the early-April weather deteriorating, we were fighting for our lives. After playing through The Loop, arguably the most stock part of the routing with 9th and 10th holes crisscrossing as they normally do, we decided that a steak roll and a Bovril were necessary before playing the 10th and 11th holes. A much-needed break from the weather, we felt refreshed for whatever new challenges lay ahead. After washing our hands in what is assuredly the hottest faucet water on the planet, we played the 10th and 11th holes (from a thrilling angle back at the Eden green) and then set back toward town, the buildings becoming more imposing with each passing shot, and the weather deteriorating further. The 14th hole, like the 5th, was easily a highlight of the day. A par five, the wind rips off the left side of the fairway with the Seven Sisters guarding it and the Hell bunker lurking up the middle, playing to the back half of the double green shared by the 4th and 14th holes on the normal routing, adding another 50 yards to the hole and bringing “Ginger Beer” more into play. The usual 14th follows this same corridor, but with the tee on the reverse route much farther to the right and with the short, right half of the green, this one felt a lot more free-flowing.
